key_insight: FlexPart brings different levels of user control into one image-to-3D part generation model. Users can guide generation with sparse points, bounding boxes, or masks rather than switching between specialized models.
problem_solved: Existing 3D part generation methods lack the flexibility to support workflows that require different amounts and types of geometric guidance.
method: Introduce a unified image-to-3D part generation framework with variable-granularity geometric conditions.
Support heterogeneous guidance inputs, including sparse points, bounding boxes, and masks.
Use gated adaptive modulation to integrate these different conditioning signals within a single model.
impact: The approach could make controllable 3D asset creation more adaptable to different user workflows. Practitioners could offer lightweight or detailed guidance through one generation pipeline; the provided abstract excerpt does not report quantitative results.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image and geometric guidance → FlexPart → generated 3D parts.
Control spectrum showing sparse points, bounding boxes, and masks as alternative guidance types.
Fusion diagram illustrating gated adaptive modulation combining heterogeneous inputs.
Color-coded 3D object illustration highlighting individually generated parts.
paper_title: A Unified Framework for Image-to-3D Part Generation via Variable Granularity
paper_authors: Qiwen Gu, Xin Zhou, Xiwu Chen, Zhongyang Zhu, Zhuo Zhang
